page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, tailored for high-throughput, I/O-intensive workloads. It is equipped with dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processors operating at up to 3.7 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 virtual CPUs. Hardware instruction flags include AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16) along with AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic support. Cache distribution per core architecture provides 32 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning totals 512.0 GB, maintaining an 8.0 GB-per-core ratio.

A central component of the L64as_v4 instance is its massive direct-attached local storage footprint, supplying 15,360 GB across local NVMe SSDs. Graphics processing units are absent on this profile, leaving general computation and vectorized math entirely to the AMD EPYC host processor. The platform demonstrates elevated multi-core performance metrics, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,342.0 (top 10%) and a PassMark CPU score of 75,798.99, complemented by 98,427.49 on stress-ng multi-core CPU testing.

Data-oriented benchmarks indicate strong execution across transactional and caching patterns, with Redis SET throughput recording 89.18 million operations per second and PassMark database operations reaching 27,733.64. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 150.96 GB/sec for 256 MB reads and 106.62 GB/sec for writes. The instance delivers robust efficiency when consolidating large datasets on direct local NVMe capacity rather than incurring network storage overhead, though the lack of hardware accelerators naturally bounds large language model generation speeds on heavy models. Best-fit use cases include large-scale relational databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed file systems, high-concurrency caching tiers, and static web serving.

The primary tradeoffs center around architectural specialization. Without bundled discrete GPUs, high-parameter machine learning jobs are limited to CPU-based inference, where it achieves solid prompt processing for smaller models (3,999.55 tokens/sec on 135M models) but drops significantly on 70B parameter models (3.37 tokens/sec text generation). For compute and storage consolidation, however, its balance of 64 vCPUs, 512 GB RAM, and 15.3 TB local NVMe SSDs provides high resource density for enterprise operational datastores.
description: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage-optimized instance driven by a 64-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz across 32 physical cores, accompanied by 512.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core) and 15,360 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking discrete GPUs, it relies on x86_64 AVX-512 instructions and high multi-core capacity, logging 21,342.0 points in multi-core Geekbench benchmarks and 89.18 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Memory throughput yields 106.62 GB/sec on uncached large-block writes and 150.96 GB/sec on reads. Qualitative cost efficiency is highest when leveraging the dense local NVMe storage array directly, replacing external storage overhead for throughput-demanding workloads. This configuration is particularly suited for high-transaction relational databases, distributed NoSQL platforms, caching layers, and high-concurrency web serving.
